best_for: Note takers who think in outlines and daily journals, want their knowledge base on their own disk, and are comfortable testing a beta.
description:
Logseq is an open-source app for notes and personal knowledge, run in the open on GitHub. The team says it puts privacy, long-term access to your notes and your control over them first.

In the new database version, tag any block with #Card to turn it into a flashcard for spaced review. Tag a block #Template, set it to apply to journals, and every new day's page starts with your layout. You can add properties to any block, and two pages may share a name if their tags differ, such as Apple #Company and Apple #Fruit. A deleted page can be restored for 30 days. The paid Publish feature, which needs a Sync account or your own server, shares a single page on the web with an optional password.

points.title: Outliner with linked notes
points.text: Logseq organizes notes as outlines and daily journals that link to each other. It supports Markdown and Org-mode, PDF annotation, tasks and plugins, and it is open source under the AGPL v3.

points.title: The 2.0 database version is beta
points.text: Windows and macOS here are on 2.0.2, the new database version. The project warns that data loss is possible and suggests regular backups and a separate test graph until it leaves beta.

points.title: Linux is on the older line
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is still 0.10.15, the file-based version, while Windows and macOS have moved to 2.0. Flathub describes that build as storing notes as plain-text files.

points.title: Moving to the new format
points.text: 2.0.2 improved importing file-based graphs into the database format, keeping headings, icons, journal timestamps and PDF annotation order.

points.title: Sync and phones are still early
points.text: Real-time collaboration for syncing across devices is in alpha. An iOS beta is in testing, and Android is listed as coming soon. A web app runs at app.logseq.com.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 94 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers in per-user and machine-wide forms. macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later) and Linux list only the current release. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub.
